title: Introduce anticipatory buffered autoscaler and utilization-reporting agent
author: Jordan Park
release_notes: Adds a new anticipatory buffered autoscaler that keeps a small warm buffer for predicted short spikes and a low-cardinality utilization-reporting agent to improve tenant telemetry without inflating metrics cardinality. No customer-visible API changes; rollout controlled via feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets observed recurring short-duration spike patterns that cause repeated cold allocations and transient SLO violations for small-to-medium tenants. Existing autoscaler reacts late and either overprovisions long tails or allows brief latency spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an anticipatory buffered autoscaler (ABA) that maintains a small, decaying warm buffer based on short-term workload forecasts and headroom signals, and (2) a utilization-reporting agent that aggregates per-tenant utilization into percentile buckets and sampled histograms to reduce cardinality while preserving signal quality.

Design summary: ABA runs as an autoscaler policy extension that watches the existing demand predictor (short-window EWMA + burst detector) and keeps a configurable buffer of N warm slots per-tenant class. Buffer sizing uses a probabilistic safety margin: buffer = ceil(P50_predicted_concurrency * alpha + min_fixed)) with decay half-life to release unused warm slots over a configurable window. The buffer is subject to a global safety cap and uses soft-decommit (graceful drain) so in-flight requests complete before returning capacity. The utilization-reporting agent samples per-device and per-tenant utilization at low frequency and reports aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p95) and a small, fixed histogram (5 buckets) to the control plane. Aggregation keys are low-cardinality (region, tenant_class, slot_type) to avoid metrics explosion.

Implementation details: - New autoscaler plugin in autoscaler/plugin/buffered_autoscaler.go with a light state machine for buffered slots and decay timers. - Predictor hook points added to autoscaler/dispatcher so ABA can observe short-window forecasts without copying core logic. - Soft-decommit implemented as graceful-eviction in orchestrator/evict.go with a 30s default drain window and immediate preemption override for hard safety events. - Util-report agent implemented in telemetry/agent/util_reporter.go; uses local reservoir sampling and per-period aggregation; flushes to control plane via existing telemetry client with a new compact proto. - Feature flag: feature/aba_enabled (defaults to off). Cluster-wide knobs available in config/dedicated.yaml.

Config knobs (defaults): - aba_enabled: false - aba_per_tenant_min_buffer: 1 - aba_alpha: 0.25 - aba_decay_half_life_s: 300 - aba_global_cap_percent: 0.03 - aba_drain_window_s: 30 - util_report_period_s: 60 - util_sample_rate: 0.05

Test plan and results: Unit tests added for buffer math and decay (autoscaler/plugin/buffered_autoscaler_test.go), soft-decommit lifecycle, and telemetry aggregation. Integration tests in perf-canary simulate rapid 10s spikes and validate that ABA reduces cold allocations. In staging runs with a mix of 120 tenants: - Cold allocation events reduced by ~34% compared to baseline autoscaler. - 95th token-start latency for small tenants dropped from median 220ms -> 155ms on staging workload. - Median cluster idle capacity changed by +0.8% (within target). Telemetry bandwidth measured at +2.1% due to util_reporter; cardinality remained stable.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable ABA in a single region (us-west-2) for test clusters for 48h. 3) Enable for a small tenant-class (non-critical). 4) Monitor eviction/cold-start and p95 latency. 5) Gradual ramp with canary to all dedicated clusters. If regressions observed: flip aba_enabled=false and let buffers decay, or reduce aba_alpha and aba_per_tenant_min_buffer.

Related: Linear ENG-4921 (anticipatory autoscaling investigation), ENG-5002 (reduce cold allocations for SMB tenants).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf canary - [x] Feature-flagged roll out - [x] Observability dashboards updated

Upgrade notes: No DB migrations. Config defaults keep feature off. Operators should pre-seed config with aba_global_cap_percent if operating close to capacity.

Security: telemetry payload uses existing encrypted channel; payload size limited. No tenant secrets added.

Ops note: The util_reporter runs on control-plane-adjacent agents; it may add a small CPU percent to telemetry agent (~1-2%). This is configurable via util_sample_rate.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Please clarify global cap interaction with dedicated reservations. Are we allowed to exceed tenant reservations temporarily?

Jordan Park: Reply: ABA never exceeds tenant reservation limits; global cap is a safety layer to avoid cluster-wide warm buffers consuming more than X% of total capacity. Added explicit assertion and unit test.
Carlos Mendez: Code looks good, but the decay math seems aggressive for very bursty tenants. Can we expose half-life per-tenant class?
Jordan Park: Reply: Added aba_decay_half_life_s override per tenant_class and updated config docs. Kept default conservative (300s).
Riley Patel: CI flaked on telemetry proto generation; reran and passed. Please add a canary dashboard tile before merging.
Jordan Park: Reply: Added dashboard JSON and a short runbook for interpreting p50/p95 util signals.
testing: Unit + integration tests included. Perf canary run against staging with waveform traffic. Manual verification steps listed in docs/runbooks/aba_runbook.md.
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind aba_enabled=false. Operators can enable gradually. Dashboard and runbook included in release bundle.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag in canary region per rollout plan, monitor dashboards: aba/cold_alloc_reduction, aba/per_tenant_buffer_usage, telemetry/util_percentiles.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: small steady-state increase in idle slots if alpha too large. Mitigation: global cap and decay, default conservative alpha, immediate feature flag off for rollback.
